title: Impact of Dividend Initiation on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event Study.  
Why: We observe daily returns for multiple firms around an exogenous announcement date (dividend initiation).  Abnormal returns (AR) relative to a market model isolate the surprise component of the news.  Averaging AR on the event day and summing them in a short window (CAR) delivers the causal effect of the announcement under:  

Key assumptions  
1. Market-model validity – the expected return E[ret] = α + β·mkt_ret outside the event window.  
2. No other confounding firm–specific news in the narrow event window (−1,+1).  
3. No information leakage (AR≈0 before the event) and no anticipation/overlap across firms.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Event-study: Dividend initiation announcement
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(broom)
})

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s53_data.csv"
df   <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2. Abnormal return (market-model) ---------------------------------
df <- df %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# 3. Average Abnormal Return on announcement day (day 0) ------------
ar0      <- df %>% filter(event_day == 0) %>% pull(AR)
tt_ar0   <- t.test(ar0)

# 4. Cumulative Abnormal Return (-1,+1) ------------------------------
car      <- df %>% 
             filter(event_day >= -1, event_day <= 1) %>% 
             group_by(stock_id) %>% 
             summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop") %>% 
             pull(CAR)
tt_car   <- t.test(car)

# 5. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ----------------------------------------------
## 5a. Market-adjusted model (assume β = 1)
df <- df %>% mutate(AR_ma = ret - mkt_ret)

car_ma <- df %>% 
            filter(event_day >= -1, event_day <= 1) %>% 
            group_by(stock_id) %>% 
            summarise(CAR_ma = sum(AR_ma), .groups = "drop") %>% 
            pull(CAR_ma)
tt_car_ma <- t.test(car_ma)

## 5b. Placebo window (-10,-5): should be ≈0
placebo <- df %>% 
            filter(event_day >= -10, event_day <= -5) %>% 
            group_by(stock_id) %>% 
            summarise(Placebo_CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop") %>% 
            pull(Placebo_CAR)
tt_placebo <- t.test(placebo)

# 6. Print results ---------------------------------------------------
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("ANNOUNCEMENT-DAY EFFECT\n")
cat("Average Abnormal Return day 0  :", round(mean(ar0)*100, 3), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic =", round(tt_ar0$statistic, 3),
    "  p-value =", round(tt_ar0$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

cat("Cumulative Abnormal Return (-1,+1):\n")
cat("Mean CAR =", round(mean(car)*100, 3), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic =", round(tt_car$statistic, 3),
    "  p-value =", round(tt_car$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

cat("ROBUSTNESS 1 – Market-adjusted CAR (-1,+1):\n")
cat("Mean =", round(mean(car_ma)*100, 3), "%,  p =", 
    round(tt_car_ma$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

cat("ROBUSTNESS 2 – Placebo window (-10,-5):\n")
cat("Mean =", round(mean(placebo)*100, 3), "%,  p =", 
    round(tt_placebo$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Dividend initiations usually signal management’s confidence in stable future cash flows, so the market reaction is typically positive.  
I expect:  
• AAR₀ ≈ +1 % (0.8–1.5 %) with a t-statistic ≈ 3–4.  
• CAR(−1,+1) ≈ +2 % (1.5–2.5 %), highly significant.  
Robustness checks should yield similar positive CAR using the market-adjusted model, while the placebo window should be statistically indistinguishable from zero, supporting the exogeneity and no-leakage assumptions.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare CAR on announcement day to pre-announcement days.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Dividend initiation announcements lead to a negative CAR on the announcement day.
